content: Hey! I could really use some advice. I’ve been invited to my high school friend’s baby shower in Minneapolis, but I was planning to take a mental health break that weekend after a super intense project at work. It’s tricky, though, because she keeps mentioning how much it would mean if I could come. What do you think?
You can't please everyone. You're allowed to say no.

I get that, but it feels different when it’s a close friend. I don’t want to let her down or damage our friendship over something that probably means a lot to her. At the same time, I really need this break after pushing myself so hard at work. I just wish there was a way to handle this without feeling guilty.
It's okay to take care of your mental health. It's also okay to say no to an event. You can still be a good friend even if you can't attend.

I hear you, but I worry about the long-term impact of saying no. We’ve been friends for so long, and I really value that connection. If I miss this event, will she feel abandoned or think I’m not there for her during a big moment in her life? I just want to balance taking care of myself with being a supportive friend.

It's important to prioritize your own mental health while also being a supportive friend. You can still be there for your friend in other ways, such as sending a gift or a card, or offering to help her in the future when she has a baby.

That’s a good point, and I do want to be supportive. I could definitely send a thoughtful gift or a heartfelt message. But I still feel a bit uneasy about it—like if she really wants me there, I might be seen as not fully being there for her when she needs friends the most. I guess I'm just stuck on how to balance my need for rest and her expectations of friendship.

It's important to communicate with your friend and explain your situation. You can say that you understand how important the event is to her, but you need to prioritize your own mental health. It's okay to have boundaries in friendships.

That makes sense, but I'm really worried about how she'll take it. I can already picture her being disappointed, and I hate the thought of letting her down. I guess it just feels easier to come up with a quick excuse instead of having a potentially tough conversation. But maybe being honest is the better long-term solution? What do you think?

It's always better to be honest with your friends. It may be difficult at first, but it's important to communicate your needs and boundaries. Your friend may be disappointed, but she'll appreciate your honesty in the long run.

You’re probably right. Being upfront would likely show that I care, even if I can’t make it. I just keep second-guessing if it really is that big of a deal for her. Maybe if I explain how much I’ve been through lately at work, she’ll understand? It's just hard to find the right words without feeling like I'm making excuses.

It's important to be honest about your situation, but also be respectful of your friend's feelings. You can say that you've been going through a lot at work and need to take some time for yourself, but also express how much you value your friendship with her.

That's a solid approach. I could definitely convey how much I care while also being clear about needing that time. I guess I’ll also want to offer my support in other ways, like checking in with her after the shower. It’s just tricky to figure out how to phrase everything so she knows it’s about self-care and not about her. Any tips on how to start that message?

You can start the message by expressing your excitement for her upcoming baby shower, and then explain that you've been going through a lot lately at work and need to take some time for yourself. You can also mention that you still value your friendship and want to be there for her in other ways, such as checking in with her after the event.

That’s a great framework! I could start with something positive about how excited I am for her and how special this time is. Then I can smoothly mention my need for a break. I like the idea of emphasizing that I'll still be there for her after—maybe I can even suggest a coffee date to celebrate her and catch up later. Thanks for helping me figure this out!
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. Remember, it's important to be honest and respectful in your conversation with your friend. Good luck!
Thanks! I feel a bit more confident about approaching her now. I’ll make sure to send that message soon. I appreciate your support! It’s just nice to have someone to bounce these thoughts off of.
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any more questions or need further advice, feel free to ask. Good luck with your conversation with your friend!
I will, thanks! Just one last thing—if she does respond negatively or seems hurt, how do I handle that? I want to make sure I respond in a way that reassures her while staying true to my boundaries.

If she responds negatively or seems hurt, it's important to listen to her feelings and show empathy. You can apologize for any hurt you've caused and reiterate that you still value your friendship. You can also explain your reasons for needing a break and reassure her that you'll still be there for her in other ways. It's important to stay true to your boundaries, but also be respectful of her feelings.
